thread:
Mira: Pushed neon20b-int4 v1 to canary in us-west-2. Quick smoke looks fine but we saw 3 OOMs in the last hour when microbatch=4 and max_new_tokens=512. Mem fragmentation spikes before the OOM.
Devin: Can you paste the exact cmd and logs? is this hotstart or coldstart?
Mira: hotstart mostly. Command: `rwdctl serve --model neon20b-int4 --batch-size 4 --max-new-tokens 512 --prefetch true`. Attached a short log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-01T14:22:10Z] alloc failed: cudaMalloc 0x7faa.. size=120MB
[2026-03-01T14:22:10Z] kv_cache_alloc: used=11.2GB free=1.1GB
[2026-03-01T14:22:10Z] slab_compactor: triggered compaction round=2 reclaimed=24MB
[2026-03-01T14:22:11Z] runtime: OOM
```
Mira: Note frag looks like many small frees and some slab churn right before OOM.
Jon: Initial thought: neon20b's attention kernel for long seqs temporarily peaks allocation. Two quick mitigations: lower default `max_new_tokens` to 200 for this model, and reduce microbatch to 2 for canary.
Sasha: Lowering max_new_tokens on model profile sounds reasonable as a quick safety net. Any perf hit metrics if we do that?
Devin: Throughput will drop slightly for very long gens but tail latency should improve and OOMs should vanish. Also check KV eviction threshold: we currently evict only when free < 5%, maybe bump to 8% for this model.
Mira: Running canary with microbatch=2 and `kv_evict_percent=8` now. Will monitor.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: neon20b-int4 canary config updated by Mira (microbatch -> 2, kv_evict_percent -> 8). :white_check_mark:
Devin: Also try enabling `prefetch=false` to reduce simultaneous allocations during tokenization/first-step.
Mira: Good call. toggling prefetch off for one host to compare.
Jon: For postmortem: add a quick eval comparing generation quality at max_new_tokens 512 vs 200 on our long-form prompt set (doc_summarize_long). If quality delta < 1% then keep 200 as default.
Sasha: I'll run the eval harness. Sending prompt sample: `<<article>> TL;DR in 5 bullets, preserve dates and numeric facts.`
Mira: Early results: with microbatch=2 + kv_evict=8 + prefetch=false, no OOMs in 2 hours stress. Latency tail improved ~150ms.
Devin: Nice. If stable, we should push a model-profile default change and add an annotation in the model catalog explaining the max_new_tokens tradeoff.
Jon: Agree. Also create a short runbook entry: steps to triage neon20b OOMs (check slab_compactor logs, kv free %, toggles to try).
Sasha: I'll draft the runbook and the eval report and link back here.
Mira: Thanks — will keep canary running overnight and update tomorrow morning. :coffee:
